Under a single frozen vision-language backbone shared by all compared systems, attains the best SR and SPL in every setting---59.9 /31.8 on HM3D v0.1, 71.0 /31.5 on HM3D v0.2, and 46.6 /16.6 on MP3D---with SR gains of up to 4.9 points and structured retrieval contributing up to 2.8 SPL points. The code is available in https://github.com/startracker0/htce.git Cross-scene object navigation, homeomorphism-inspired canonicalization, semantic graph matching, visual-topological memory, vision-language models. Introduction sec:introduction bject -goal navigation requires embodied agents to locate target objects in unfamiliar environments using partial observations anderson2018evaluation,batra2020objectnav,majumdar2022zson,nie2025wmnav,chaplot2020object,gervet2023navigating . As agents navigate across different residential environments, they can accumulate successful experiences that record target encounters and the semantic approaches leading to them khanna2024goatbench,wang2026trajrag . Although these environments differ in appearance and geometric layout, successful navigation approaches may exhibit recurring semantic structures, such as reaching a target in a bedroom through a passage from a living room wu2019bayesian . Such similarities suggest that historical navigation experiences may provide useful guidance for object searches in new environments. Establishing such correspondences remains challenging because semantically similar navigation approaches may yield different graph representations. A passage described as a hallway in one scene may appear as an entryway followed by a corridor in another, while repeated observations may introduce additional intermediate vertices. These variations affect semantic descriptions and topological granularity without necessarily altering the underlying navigation structure. Conversely, changes in meaningful semantic regions, branching connections, or goal endpoints may distinguish different navigation approaches. Therefore, cross-scene experience matching should accommodate representational variations while preserving navigation-relevant structural distinctions. Graph homeomorphism offers a natural perspective for handling topological variations, as edge subdivision introduces intermediate degree-two vertices without changing the underlying connectivity diestel2017 . Applying this principle to navigation experience graphs requires additional semantic constraints, since not all intermediate vertices can be treated as removable subdivisions. For example, transition vertices along nonbranching passages may be suppressed, whereas semantic regions, junctions, and navigation endpoints must remain explicit. Building on this principle, we introduce , a homeomorphism-inspired topological framework for cross-scene navigation experience canonicalization and reuse. The framework characterizes representational variations through two complementary operations: feature subdivision, which captures compatible semantic descriptions, and topology subdivision, which accounts for intermediate transition vertices along nonbranching passages. Through feature canonicalization and semantically constrained topological reduction, constructs comparable semantic sequences and structural signatures while preserving semantic anchors, branching relations, and navigation endpoints. As illustrated in Fig.~ fig:motivation , approaches represented at different granularities can be structurally aligned without removing meaningful branches. We further integrate with persistent navigation memory to support cross-scene experience reuse zheng2024esceme,wang2026trajrag . Across successive navigation episodes, the agent stores successful navigation approaches and associated target observations. Based on the reduced representations, subdivision-aware approximate matching retrieves relevant historical experiences as semantic guidance for a frozen vision-language model (VLM) bai2025qwen3vl , while action selection remains grounded in current visual observations nie2025wmnav,goetting2025end . We report navigation comparisons on HM3D and MP3D ramakrishnan2021hm3d,yadav2023hm3dsem,chang2017matterport3d,savva2019habitat and conduct recorded-route and controlled-graph analyses to examine the structural properties of the proposed representation. A canonicalization that preserves navigation structure should deliver compression without loss, and we establish both halves. Collapsing admissible subdivisions makes stored experiences comparable and the index compact, while the information the policy acts on is retained intact: reduction merges distinct descriptions of the same approach and leaves task performance at full strength. This is lossless compression of navigation experience, and it is what makes a single canonical index reusable across scenes. Our main contributions are summarized as follows: Homeomorphism-inspired canonicalization. We introduce a homeomorphism-inspired topological framework that characterizes compatible feature and topology subdivisions and defines structural correspondence between navigation experiences while preserving semantic anchors, branching relations, and navigation endpoints. Subdivision-aware graph matching. We develop feature canonicalization and semantically constrained topological reduction to construct comparable semantic sequences and structural signatures for approximate matching of navigation approaches. Cross-scene navigation experience reuse. We integrate subdivision-aware matching with persistent navigation memory and a frozen vision-language model, and show that canonicalization compresses the experience index losslessly: it merges 17.7--23.6 of stored descriptions and satisfies every prescribed invariance and sensitivity relation while retaining full task performance, with structured retrieval contributing up to 2.8 SPL points. Related Work sec:related Object Navigation With Foundation Models Foundation models support object navigation by connecting visual observations with semantic goals zhou2023esc,huang2023vlmaps . L3MVN and OpenFMNav leverage language and vision-language priors for exploration yu2023l3mvn,kuang2024openfmnav , while VLFM uses visual-semantic relevance to guide frontier exploration yokoyama2024vlfm . VLMNav and WMNav further employ vision-language reasoning for navigation decisions goetting2025end,nie2025wmnav . Rather than introducing a new navigation policy, provides a frozen VLM with structural guidance retrieved from successful historical experiences. Navigation Memory, Scene Graphs, and Experience Retrieval sec:related_memory Topological memories represent spatial connectivity for navigation savinov2018semiparametric,an2025etpnav,chaplot2020neural . These methods maintain graph structures over observations but do not explicitly handle variations in region naming or observation granularity across scenes. Semantic scene graphs further support object- and region-level reasoning yin2024sgnav,loo2025openscenegraphs,armeni2019scene,gu2024conceptgraphs . UniGoal employs scene-goal graph matching for exploration, and SSMG-Nav organizes persistent semantic memory through spatial keypoints yin2025unigoal,niu2026ssmgnav . Navigation memory extends perception beyond current observations zheng2024esceme,li2024memonav,zhang2025mem2ego,fang2019scene . GOAT-Bench evaluates memory use across successive navigation goals khanna2024goatbench , while TrajRAG retrieves historical geometric-semantic trajectories through hierarchical retrieval with a trained trajectory encoder wang2026trajrag . Beyond navigation, graph edit distance supports comparison between nonidentical graphs gao2010survey,riesen2009approximate , and graph homeomorphism characterizes connectivity preserved under edge subdivision diestel2017 . Several recent methods accumulate experience across episodes or scenes. GOAT-Bench benchmarks lifelong multi-goal navigation with persistent memory khanna2024goatbench . TrajRAG retrieves cross-episode geometric-semantic trajectories using contrastive-trained embeddings wang2026trajrag . C-NAV addresses continual object navigation in open worlds with self-evolving category knowledge yu2025cnav , and EvolveNav uses proactive preflection and self-evolving memory for zero-shot navigation chai2026evolvenav . Unlike these approaches, uses homeomorphism-inspired topological canonicalization to align different-granularity graph representations before matching: compatible passage labels are normalized and intermediate degree-two transitions are suppressed, producing a canonical form that absorbs naming and observation-frequency variations while preserving meaningful semantic anchors, branching relations, and navigation endpoints. This makes cross-scene matching invariant to representational differences that do not alter the navigation structure. The matcher is also comparatively light: UniGoal drives its scene--goal graph matching with a LLaVA, LLaMA, and CLIP stack, and TrajRAG trains a contrastive trajectory encoder on top of GroundingDINO, MobileSAM, and a Qwen3-32B planner, whereas performs training-free matching over a single frozen VLM backbone shared by all prompt roles. Preliminary sec:setting VLM Backbone Each object-navigation episode specifies an indoor scene, an initial state, and a target category . At time , the agent receives an RGB-D observation and local pose information. A depth-based action proposer generates visible action candidates , and the controller executes the candidate selected by the policy goetting2025end . A single frozen VLM backbone handles perception, prediction, planning, and action selection through separate prompt contexts nie2025wmnav . The backbone parameters remain fixed throughout all episodes; this work does not fine-tune the VLM. Let denote the extracted visual-semantic record. Memory updating, experience retrieval, and action selection are expressed as Here writes the record into memory , retrieves guidance containing target evidence and semantic navigation guidance, and is the frozen VLM policy with parameters . Executable actions remain grounded in current observations. Cross-Scene Experience Reuse Protocol sec:reuse_protocol Navigation episodes are processed across different scenes with persistent experience memory khanna2024goatbench,wang2026trajrag,yu2025cnav . Episode reset reinitializes the active region chain, previous action, and odometry. Persistent snapshots store region observations, graph connections, target evidence, and successful approaches; their visibility in the next episode follows the configured load and save lifecycle. Successful approaches are associated with target records using terminal evaluator feedback. Multiple workers process assigned episode sequences concurrently. Each maintains a working graph and exchanges persistent snapshots at episode boundaries.

title: FloMo: 3D Scene Flow as a World Action Model Intermediate for Learning from Human Video
summary: Pretrained video generation models distill internet-scale motion priors into robot policies, but full video is a redundant signal for action prediction. We argue that dense 3D motion is the medium through which video pretraining best transfers to robot actions, and that predicting motion rather than video affords better sample-efficiency for action prediction. FloMo is a 5B video-generation model fine-tuned to predict 3D scene-flow and action tokens. Rendering scene flow as RGB and encoding it into the same latent space as video enables a pretrained video generation backbone to efficiently adapt to predict 3D scene flow. Co-trained on action-free human video and action-labeled robot teleoperation data, our model benefits from human-video pretraining and generalizes to unseen objects, motion primitives, and tasks. Replacing motion prediction with a video prediction objective degrades out-of-distribution generalization, while adding a video prediction target alongside motion lowers policy success rather than improving it. When motion, video, and action are predicted jointly, action tokens attend far more to motion than to video, suggesting that predicting video wastes model capacity. Together, these results indicate that motion effectively mediates the transfer from video pretraining to action. More information can be found at flomo-wam.github.io.
full_text: Pretrained video generation models distill internet-scale motion priors into robot policies, but full video is a redundant signal for action prediction. We argue that dense 3D motion is the medium through which video pretraining best transfers to robot actions, and that predicting motion rather than video affords better sample-efficiency for action prediction. is a 5B video-generation model fine-tuned to predict 3D scene-flow and action tokens. Rendering scene flow as RGB and encoding it into the same latent space as video enables a pretrained video generation backbone to efficiently adapt to predict 3D scene flow. Co-trained on action-free human video and action-labeled robot teleoperation data, our model benefits from human-video pretraining and generalizes to unseen objects, motion primitives, and tasks. Replacing motion prediction with a video prediction objective degrades out-of-distribution generalization, while adding a video prediction target alongside motion lowers policy success rather than improving it. When motion, video, and action are predicted jointly, action tokens attend far more to motion than to video, suggesting that predicting video wastes model capacity. Together, these results indicate that motion effectively mediates the transfer from video pretraining to action. More information can be found at flomo-icra.github.io . Introduction sec:intro Pretrained video generation models can be used to distill internet-scale motion priors into robot policies. Transfer from video to action is typically attributed to information overlap between RGB videos and the actions that produce them: a model that predicts the world's next pixels has implicitly learned the dynamics that link action to outcome~ Jang2025DreamGen, Liang2025VideoPolicy, Ye2026DreamZero . Video, however, is a far higher-entropy signal than the action it implies. Videos that differ in texture, lighting, material, and background depict the same underlying motion and imply the same action, so a world action model (WAM) trained to predict pixels spends capacity on appearance that action prediction never uses~ Wen2024ATM, Collins2025AMPLIFY, Xu2024Im2Flow2Act . WAMs vary on how tightly they couple the video backbone to the action head, but they share a prediction target: future pixels. We question this assumption and ask: which prediction target lets video pretraining transfer to action most directly? We argue that the answer is 3D motion. Given the current observation, the action that produces a future state depends on how the scene transformed rather than on appearance and texture. Predicted frames that differ only in lighting or background share the same motion and imply the same action. Predicting motion rather than pixels hence targets a lower-entropy signal and incorporates this invariance instead of forcing the model to learn it, leaving the action head a tighter information bottleneck it can decode directly. Our insight is that a pretrained video VAE already provides a latent space for motion. We represent motion as the 3D displacement of each tracked scene point over time in a canonical frame independent of camera motion, otherwise known as 3D scene flow, and render this vector field as an RGB image. Rendering scene flow as RGB lets us encode it with a pretrained video VAE, giving scene-flow tokens the same latent representation format as video without needing to train a new tokenizer. This lets us finetune only the backbone to predict motion. We instantiate this in , a Wan~2.2 5B DiT that, given an image and language instruction, flow-matches 3D scene-flow and action tokens, with scene flow encoded into the same video latent space the model was pretrained on. We co-train on action-free human video and action-labeled robot teleoperation data, and find that predicting motion alone improves both in-distribution policy success and out-of-distribution generalization, relative to predicting video or predicting video and motion jointly. Our contributions are: Motion as a WAM prediction target ( sec:method ). We argue that WAMs should predict motion rather than video: motion is a lower-complexity, texture-invariant target an action head can decode directly, and the priors of video pretraining are carried by the pretrained backbone, not by the prediction target. We realize this by rendering 3D scene flow as an RGB image and encoding it with the pretrained video VAE, so scene-flow tokens share the video latent space and a single backbone flow-matches motion and action without a new tokenizer. Motion is the most effective prediction target for policy learning ( sec:in-dist , sec:ood ). Across real-robot manipulation, predicting motion yields higher in-distribution success and out-of-distribution generalization than predicting video or jointly predicting video and motion; adding a video target interferes with action learning rather than complementing it. Generalization from human video ( sec:human-video ). Our model generalizes to objects, motion primitives, and tasks seen only in human data. Related Work sec:related Learning Robot Policies from Action-Free Videos Action-labeled robot demonstrations are expensive, while large-scale action-free videos of humans, robots, and objects are abundant. One line of work uses passive video to pretrain visual representations, rewards, or value functions ( Nair2022R3M , Ma2022VIP , Bhateja2023VPTR , Dashora2025ViVa ). These methods improve data efficiency but do not learn explicit predictive models of future dynamics. Another line of work learns latent actions or transition variables from unlabeled videos through self-supervised objectives such as future prediction, frame consistency, or reconstruction ( Bruce2024Genie , Ye2024LAPA , Chen2024Moto ). While these methods reduce reliance on action labels, their latents may encode visual information useful for reconstruction but unnecessary for control. Finally, work on learning from human videos studies cross-embodiment alignment or explicit retargeting to transfer human demonstrations to robots ( Punamiya2025EgoBridge , Kareer2024EgoMimic , Kim2025UniSkill , Li2024OKAMI , Dan2025XSim ). These works focus on bridging the human-robot embodiment gap; our work instead focuses on the prediction target inside of a WAM. Motion and Geometry-Aware Video Prediction Raw pixel prediction is an expensive and indirect objective for learning physical dynamics, motivating methods that introduce motion or geometric intermediates. Some use 2D motion as an interface between action-free video and robot actions, predicting future image-point trajectories and conditioning policies on them ( Wen2024ATM , Collins2025AMPLIFY ). Others use flow or motion fields as an interface linking video prediction and manipulation ( Yuan2024GeneralFlow , Xu2024Im2Flow2Act , Lin2024FlowRetrieval , Gao2024FLIP ), or separate motion and temporal reasoning from appearance and camera movement in video generation ( Liu2026MoRight ). Closest to our representation choice are methods that model dynamic scenes with compact trace spaces, 3D scene flow, or point-track representations ( Lee2025TraceGen , Guo2025FlowDreamer , Hung2026ThreePoinTr ). These works show that 3D motion fields are a natural substrate for future dynamics prediction. Rather than building a bespoke latent space for motion, we render scene flow into a pretrained video-generation latent space. World Action Models Pretrained video-generation models provide motion priors for robot learning because they are trained on large-scale videos of physical interactions and object motion. Recent work uses these models for control by coupling future video prediction with action generation. One family generates task-conditioned robot videos and then recovers or co-generates actions through inverse dynamics models or latent actions ( Du2023UniPi , Ko2024AVDC , Jang2025DreamGen , Liang2025VideoPolicy ). These approaches preserve the pretrained video model, but deployment is expensive and performance depends heavily on video fidelity. A second family avoids explicit video rollout at test time by extracting intermediate latents from a pretrained video backbone and training an action head on top ( Wen2024VidMan , Hu2024VPP , Pai2025MimicVideo ). This reduces inference cost, but action prediction remains limited by the quality of the extracted video features. More tightly coupled world action models jointly model visual features and actions with shared or entangled architectures ( Zhu2025UWM , Li2025UVA , Kim2026CosmosPolicy , Ye2026DreamZero , Yuan2026FastWAM ). Our work studies a complementary axis: what future state should the world model predict? title: High-fidelity training-free photovoltaic module mapping from multi-view UAV imagery
summary: High-fidelity photovoltaic (PV) module mapping requires complete instance recovery and accurate delineation. Vision foundation models offer zero-shot segmentation, but converting incomplete and inconsistent predictions across views into a complete, geometrically accurate map of individual modules remains challenging. We propose the Multi-View PV Module Mapper (MV-PVMapper), a training-free framework coupling vision foundation models with unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) photogrammetry. First, Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) generates candidates from original images using text prompts. Their contours are then transferred into object space through per-module slope correction to limit distortion from surface-model noise, and verified against representative module dimensions to guide cross-view instance selection. Finally, accepted instances return to all covering images as box prompts for SAM~3, supplementing text prompts with spatial cues for iterative segmentation, verification and fusion. On five-direction surveys of three operational rooftop PV plants at approximately 1 cm nadir ground sampling distance, two feedback iterations recover 7,710 of 7,711 reference modules with no false positives at an intersection-over-union (IoU) matching threshold of 0.5. Macro-averaged area precision and recall reach 99.00 % and 98.52 %, respectively. Averaged across sites, the aggregated Jaccard index reaches 97.55 %, compared with 60.73 % and 41.24 % for orthomosaic segmentation and multi-view pixel-voting baselines, respectively; average precision at the stricter IoU threshold of 0.95 reaches 95.67 %. Ablation studies show that module-size constraints are critical for instance separation, while slope correction and feedback to all covering views improve boundary accuracy. These results are achieved without task-specific image annotation or segmentation-model weight updates.

Photovoltaic module mapping UAV photogrammetry Vision foundation models Zero-shot instance segmentation Multi-view fusion Introduction sec:intro The global energy transition is rapidly expanding the installed base of photovoltaic (PV) systems. By the end of 2025, global cumulative PV capacity had approached 3\,TW, after an estimated 698\,GW was installed in that year alone De_lEpine2026-wg . As the installed base grows, maintaining reliable performance over the lifetime of these assets requires inspection and maintenance at an increasingly large scale GALLARDOSAAVEDRA2018566,CHEN2023120579,barraz2025towards . Within large PV installations, tasks such as targeted diagnosis, repair and replacement require inspection findings to be linked to individual modules and their locations. Module-level georeferencing supports this link between image-based inspection and field operations barraz2025towards,bommes2022georeferencing . A module map provides a common spatial representation in which each module has its own boundary and location. Its quality depends on recovering the module inventory while preserving the separation and geometry of individual instances, rather than only identifying the area occupied by PV arrays. Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) surveys can cover an entire plant efficiently, but converting UAV images into such a map remains difficult. Modules are densely and repeatedly arranged, their gaps may span only a few pixels, and their apparent scale and shape change under oblique viewing. PV module mapping involves both extracting individual instances and establishing their geographic locations. Rule-based methods can avoid labelled data, but depend on assumptions about colour, line structure, shape or array layout wang2018photovoltaic,cardoso2024automated . Supervised detectors and segmentation networks can learn more flexible appearance features, but require annotated UAV images. Even domain-generalization methods rely on training data collected across different module types and imaging conditions to improve performance on unseen sites barraz2024one . Beyond recognising and delineating modules, mapping also requires their image-space detections to be placed in a common geographic frame. Photogrammetry provides this spatial reference for UAV imagery. Structure-from-motion (SfM) estimates camera poses and reconstructs scene geometry, supporting both the georeferencing of modules detected in individual images and the generation of orthomosaics. These products support different mapping workflows: modules can be extracted from a georeferenced digital orthophoto map (DOM) cardoso2024automated , or observations in multiple images can be associated and located using the reconstructed geometry bommes2022georeferencing,kozak2025detailed . Promptable visual foundation models (VFMs) offer a way to reduce the annotation burden. The Segment Anything Model (SAM) supports zero-shot transfer to new image distributions and tasks through prompts kirillov2023segment . SAM~3 further accepts concept prompts and can detect and segment instances named by a short noun phrase carion2025sam . Recent work has shown the potential of this training-free, open-vocabulary approach by formulating remote-sensing image interpretation as two-dimensional segmentation li2025segearthov3 . Within a photogrammetric workflow, the same model can be applied directly to a georeferenced DOM, so the predicted masks already have ground locations and physical extents. However, segmentation on a DOM uses a single orthorectified representation rather than explicitly combining predictions from the overlapping source images. For densely arranged PV modules, observations from different viewpoints can provide complementary evidence where individual views leave boundaries unclear. A multi-view UAV oblique survey provides overlapping images that can observe the same module from several directions, while camera poses and a digital surface model (DSM) relate these observations within a common object-space frame. In addition, PV modules within a plant commonly follow one or a few standardized size specifications, allowing representative dimensions to be established from a small number of field measurements. Using these sources jointly for module mapping, however, raises two related challenges. The first is to transfer predictions reliably into object space despite noise in the reconstructed surface, which can distort their locations and shapes. The second is to combine predictions from views with different visibility and image quality, so that complementary observations reinforce one another while conflicting results are suppressed. This study aims to achieve high-fidelity PV module mapping by combining zero-shot VFM segmentation with redundant observations from UAV photogrammetry, without task-specific training. We propose the Multi-View PV Module Mapper (MV-PVMapper), which links image-space segmentation and object-space geometric verification through iterative multi-view feedback. First, SAM~3 generates module candidates from the original images using a text concept prompt, without site-specific image annotation or segmentation-model weight updates. Second, per-module slope correction transfers candidate contours into object space while limiting deformation caused by DSM noise. Third, segmentation confidence and consistency with representative module dimensions guide cross-view fusion, retaining plausible module instances while suppressing conflicting and duplicate predictions. Finally, accepted object-space instances are projected into covering images as box prompts; the resulting masks are transferred back for geometric verification and fusion, providing updated spatial evidence for subsequent segmentation rounds. We evaluate MV-PVMapper on five-direction oblique photogrammetric data from three operational rooftop PV plants, with a nadir ground sampling distance (GSD) of approximately 1\,cm/pixel. After two feedback iterations, MV-PVMapper matches 7\,710 of the 7\,711 reference modules across all three sites, with no false positives at an intersection-over-union (IoU) threshold of 0.5. It achieves macro-averaged area precision and recall of 99.00 and 98.52 , respectively. Its macro-averaged aggregated Jaccard index (AJI) and average precision at the stricter IoU threshold of 0.95 ( ) reach 97.55 and 95.67 , compared with 60.73 and 60.51 for an orthomosaic segmentation baseline (DOM-IterSeg), and 41.24 and 27.52 for a multi-view pixel-voting baseline (MV-PixelVote). Together, these results show near-complete instance recovery and accurate delineation on the evaluated sites, rather than high pixel precision alone. The main contributions are as follows: We propose MV-PVMapper, a training-free framework that couples segmentation by a pretrained VFM with multi-view instance fusion in an iterative refinement loop for PV module mapping. By feeding geometrically verified instances back to all covering views as spatial prompts, the framework uses complementary observations to recover missed modules and refine their boundaries. We introduce a per-module slope-correction strategy for projecting PV masks from image space to object space. By adapting the projection to each module's local surface, it preserves module geometry and improves robustness to DSM noise. We convert readily available module dimensions into an object-space geometry score that guides candidate selection, cross-view association and feedback. This geometry-guided strategy suppresses over- and under-segmentation and helps limit error accumulation across iterations. Related Work sec:related We review PV extraction methods, prompting strategies for VFMs, and multi-view fusion with geometric priors. The review distinguishes task-specific learning from training-free inference and examines how spatial evidence can support instance association and delineation, providing the context for MV-PVMapper. PV Module Extraction and Mapping sec:rw-pv-detection Image-based PV extraction supports applications ranging from installation inventories to component inspection CHEN2023120579,barraz2025towards . Traditional methods identify panels through explicit appearance and geometric rules. Association between region and line primitives can support automatic template generation and matching without training samples wang2018photovoltaic . Edge detection, morphological processing and contour extraction provide another route to delineating individual panels cardoso2024automated . These methods make use of the regular appearance of PV installations, but their applicability depends on the chosen rules and thresholds. Changes in illumination, panel appearance or the visibility of narrow gaps can weaken the cues on which extraction relies. Supervised learning replaces much of this manual feature design with representations learned from task data. For UAV thermal imagery, training across different module types and acquisition conditions has been used to improve generalisation to unseen installations barraz2024one . title: Route Anything: A Study of Model and Policy Routing for General-Purpose AI Systems
summary: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) requires a method that can understand, generate, reason, and act across diverse domains and modalities. Rather than relying on a single model to master every capability, a promising path toward AGI now is to orchestrate a heterogeneous ecosystem of specialized models, tools, and policies (candidates) into a unified AI system. At the heart of this vision lies a fundamental question: how can an AI system dynamically select and coordinate the most capable candidate for each task while balancing performance and computational cost? In this work, we present Route Anything, a unified framework for studying model and policy routing across general-purpose AI systems. We develop a unified theoretical foundation that characterizes optimal routing under quality--cost trade-offs and establishes how the information available to a router determines its attainable performance. To systematically investigate routing across diverse capabilities, we first construct an omni-modal trajectory matrix spanning 25 benchmarks across language understanding, image, video, and speech generation, coding and workplace agents, and robotic manipulation, comprising 374,401 scored runs from 452 candidate configurations. Building on this framework, we train and test different routers to investigate the potential of omni-modal model routing, the capabilities of learned routers, and the conditions under which routing improves efficiency. Our results reveal substantial opportunities for capability orchestration: per-input oracle routing outperforms the best fixed candidate by 5.4 points, and learned routers outperform it by 0.3 points across 16 benchmarks, by 2.1 points on video generation, and by 1.1 points on robot manipulation while using 24% less policy time. More importantly, routing raises efficiency by 8.82x on average compared with the reference model.

The best candidate changes from input to input, so a router that chooses well is expected to match one fixed strongest candidate at a fraction of its price, or beat it by sending every input to the most suitable candidate that handles it best. title: GSCV++: Lightweight 3D Gaussian Splatting Sequence Compression via Standard Video Codecs
summary: This paper presents GSCV++, a lightweight pipeline for 3D {G}aussian {S}platting (GS) sequences {C}ompression with standard {V}ideo codecs. To meet the requirements of low-complexity and hardware compatibility from the industry, GSCV++ jointly improves preprocessing, 3D-to-2D mapping, and practical video compression configuration of GS compression. First, for preprocessing, energy-adaptive inter-frame spherical harmonic (SH) alternative current (AC) dimensionality reduction (EA-SHDR) is proposed to produces a compact and stable temporal SH AC feature space. It can reduce the data volume of following mapping and practical compression, as well as less complexity while eliminating redundant information. Second, for 3D-to-2D mapping, prior-based Inter-MiniPLAS (P-MiniPLAS) is designed to generate smooth 2D feature maps through prior-based weighting factor inference and small scale remapping. Compared with vanilla Parallel Linear Assignment Sorting (PLAS) and Morton scan, P-MiniPLAS ensures the generated 2D maps are more suitable for the video codec while maintaining a low level of computational complexity. Third, for practical compression, content-aware generalized compression (CA-GC) is developed to use a non-uniform bit-depth split for coordinate map generation, and a coding unit size selection is introduced for efficient compression complexity control, which fully exploits the performance of video codecs without involving normative changes. Experiments demonstrate that GSCV++ reports over 20\% in intra- and 60\% in inter-prediction rate-distortion gains compared with state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. GSCV++ also achieves faster 2D map generation, encoding, and decoding than other SOTA methods using the same type of video codecs. Ablation studies verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed modules and provide insights for subsequent research.

Gaussian splatting, compression, video codec Introduction D Gaussian splatting (GS) vanillaGS achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance in 3D reconstruction, as well as an impressive trade-off between generation speed and rendering quality. Different from the neural radiance field (NeRF) mildenhall2021nerf that embeds scene information into neural networks, GS represents 3D scenes using numerous primitives with multi-channel attributes, including geometric coordinates, color spherical harmonic (SH) direct current (DC), color SH alternating current (AC), opacity, scale, and rotation. The high-dimensional explicit representation imposes substantial memory and storage demands, leading to considerable attention to 3D GS compression in both academia and industry. The Moving Picture Experts Group (MPEG) has considered two approaches to compress 3D GS: A-3DGS and I-3DGS m71640 . A-3DGS uses multiview images/videos as input and generates a compact representation through an optimized reconstruction process, as in HAC chen2024hac , HAC++ chen2025hac++ , and CompGS liu2024compgs . I-3DGS takes generated 3D GS data as input, generates bitstreams, and reconstructs the symmetrical GS data, as in GGSC yang2024benchmark , LGSCV LGSCV , and HGSC huang2024hierarchical . A-3DGS and I-3DGS differ in their input requirements, optimization scope, and computational resources. Generally, A-3DGS methods can report better rate-distortion (RD) results than I-3DGS xing20253dgs , while also requiring higher encoding times and heavier computational resources. Recently, a joint industry proposal m72430 motivates lightweight GS compression through the reuse of standard video and point cloud codecs, such as HEVC sullivan2012overview and GPCC pcc-1 , to reduce deployment and development costs. Therefore, I-3DGS is regarded as a higher priority, i.e., fast track, in the current standardization stage, such as V-PCC AMD1 vpccAmd1 . In this paper, we follow the I-3DGS track and focus on reusing standard video codecs to compress preconstructed GS sequences m72430 , which involve three main steps, as shown in Fig. fig:motivation : preprocessing, 3D-to-2D mapping, and the compression module. First, given a 3D GS sample, a preprocessing step is applied to reduce the data volume by removing redundant information, such as pruning Etri-pruning, kaifa-pruning and feature dimensionality reduction pca-wg4, etri-pca . Second, 3D GS to 2D mapping is a key step for efficient GS coding via video codecs. Because standard video codecs are optimized for natural image content, their performance improves as the generated 2D maps better match the distribution of natural videos. Finally, the compression module implements the actual compression process, converting the mapped 2D maps into standard bitstreams. The current MPEG video-based GS compression anchor, i.e., GSCodec Studio li2025gscodec , uses Parallel Linear Assignment Sorting (PLAS) PLAS to convert GS into smooth 2D maps, followed by FFMPEG libx265 to perform compression. It uses a bit depth (BD) of 16 for geometric coordinates and 8 BD for other attributes to generate quantized images/videos. Based on preliminary results, GSCodec Studio performs stably and effectively on the MPEG tracked dataset. However, there are three limitations of GSCodec Studio: 1) SH AC attributes occupy the majority of the data volume, and GSCodec Studio directly converts them into 2D maps and feeds them into the video codec, which can lead to a lower compression ratio and higher coding complexity. 2) The vanilla PLAS algorithm is a heuristic algorithm that progressively reorders the GS maps from an extremely large receptive field, which is relatively time-consuming (see section sec:preli_plas for details) and difficult to converge to optimal results. For example, PLAS requires around 30 seconds on GS samples containing approximately half a million primitives. 3) For sequence compression, GSCodec Studio reuses the I-frame PLAS permutation for later frames and, therefore, assumes consistent primitive indices. If no tracked information is provided by the GS sequences, or if some preprocessing operators (e.g., pruning) destroy the tracked information, the P-frame 2D maps resemble noise-like images and incur poor inter-frame compression results, limiting the applicability of this strategy. The current study has developed methods to address the problems mentioned above. First, for preprocessing , some research has proven that SH AC illustrates high inter-channel redundancy yanghybridgs for a single GS frame. However, how to reduce inter-frame SH AC redundancy while keeping stable rendering quality still requires further study. Second, for 3D-to-2D mapping , a more efficient and lightweight 2D map generation method is proposed by LGSCV LGSCV , in which the two-stage Morton initialization and MiniPLAS are utilized. However, it also only considers the all-intra case. Third, for sequence compression, GSCV GSCV proposes an inter-PLAS algorithm to build the track information between adjacent frames, which is more robust to different GS sequences. However, inter-PLAS significantly increases the computational complexity; a more efficient correspondence reconstruction is desired. To develop a more effective and lightweight GS sequence compression framework, we propose GSCV++ to improve the RD and processing-time trade-off without supplied inter-frame tracked information. First, we design an energy-adaptive inter-frame SH AC dimensionality reduction (EA-SHDR) module. Based on principal component analysis (PCA), EA-SHDR selects an I-frame dimension using explained variance and reuses the basis and mean for the following frames, which can extend earlier all-intra dimensionality reduction LGSCV,pca-wg4 to a common and stable feature space within a GoP in an extremely low-complexity implementation. Second, a prior-based Inter-MiniPLAS refinement (P-MiniPLAS) is proposed to realize fast and smooth 2D map generation for inter-mode. P-MiniPLAS is a variation of vanilla PLAS, which consists of two main enhancements: First, vanilla PLAS assigns equal weighting factors to all the GS attributes during the reordering process, meaning that all selected features use the same scaling factor in the reordering objective. However, GS attributes have different importance in terms of rendering quality, as well as different sensitivities to lossy compression adcgs++ . Generally, for certain GS attributes, the smoother the 2D map is, the fewer bits are needed after compression. Therefore, inspired by the rate control study Q-domain , we interpret the reordering process of PLAS as a form of bitrate pre-allocation across different GS attributes. In light of the lack of a universal rate control approach yifan-gstrans or loss function mped for GS attributes, we use the initial attribute data volume and the quantization parameter (QP) as the priors to infer weighting factors for the reordering operation. Second, the 2D map reordering process is different for I- and P-frames. For I-frames, P-MiniPLAS inherits the strategy of the two-stage Morton scan and MiniPLAS LGSCV to generate the block-wise 2D maps (see section sec:perli_lgscv for details), while the prior-based weighting factors are introduced to enhance the MiniPLAS performance. For P-frames, we initialize block-wise 2D maps via the two-stage Morton scan first, followed by Inter-MiniPLAS to refine them. Specifically, Inter-MiniPLAS uses the I-frame 2D maps as an anchor and predefines a maximum block size (MBS). A finite set of block sizes, selected based on MBS and conforming to the coding unit (CU) sizes supported by the standard video codecs, is used to refine P-frame block-wise maps. Using P-MiniPLAS, a small scale of reordering can generate close I- and P-frame GS maps, leading to highly efficient inter-prediction. For the compression module, we propose a content-aware generalized compression (CA-GC), in which two techniques are introduced. CA-GC is based on the compression framework designed by GSCV GSCV , in which 20 BD and 10 BD are used to quantize geometry coordinates and other attributes (see section sec:perli_gscv ). GA-GC replaces the uniform 10:10 coordinate split with a non-uniform split, such as 16:4 and 12:8. The most significant bit (MSB) maps use video coding, while the least significant bit (LSB) coding choice can depend on the compression mode and split. Second, we couple the encoder's maximum CU selection with the MBS selection in P-MiniPLAS, achieving stable and robust encoding complexity control of real compression. We also optimize the implementation of CA-GC to be compatible with multiple prevalent video codecs and platforms, including HM18.0 HM , VTM23.11 VTM , FFMPEG libx265, and FFMPEG libx264 ffmpeg . Based on the proposed GSCV++, we conducted a serial experiment and ablation study on both the MPEG and Audio Video Coding Standard Workgroup of China (AVS) GS sequences. The results show that GSCV++ can report significant gains in both intra- and inter-prediction modes compared to the SOTA method; e.g., the gains over GSCV are approximately 39.6 and 68.7 on MPEG data in all-intra and inter modes, respectively. Besides, GSCV++ requires less time to generate GS 2D maps, decreasing from 24.78 to 4.58 seconds for I-frames and from 74.60 to 14.67 seconds for P-frames. Last but not least, GSCV++ reports faster encoding and decoding speeds than GSCV and GSCodec Studio when using the same type of downstream codecs, indicating that the 2D videos generated by GSCV++ are smoother. The contributions are summarized as follows: We propose a comprehensive 3D GS sequence compression method, GSCV++, which can achieve SOTA compression performance, as well as lightweight 2D map generation and fast coding speed.
